terra.problem: The passage does not say that nobody planned for Ahaziah to become king.
The modern comparison about what a mom says breaks the rule against modern parent scenarios.
The joke about trusting a confident-looking drawer does not make sense in his backstory or as a comparison to taking counsel.
Identifying Mesha as a king of Moab is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Identifying Sennacherib as a king of Assyria needs an outside reference. Also, 'Wrong king' says wrong about the baker's answer.
The passage does not say Ahaziah sent no message or did not go home.
The passage does not establish that sending a letter would have kept Ahaziah safe or changed what happened to him.
The passage does not say going home was an option Ahaziah declined or that Jerusalem had to wait.
Saying the writer does not add more overlooks the rest of verse 7, which tells of Ahaziah going out with Joram to meet Jehu.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage says Ahaziah went out with Joram to meet Jehu; it does not say he walked right up to him on that occasion.
The passage says Ahaziah went out with Joram to meet Jehu. 'Met him anyway' also suggests Ahaziah knew Jehu's mission, which the text does not say.
The passage states what Jehu was anointed to do; it does not say he was never sent to rebuild anything.
The joke about hiding makes light of Ahaziah being pursued and captured before his death.
The passage says no one was left with the strength to rule, not that nobody in his house was left to take the throne.
The passage limits the statement to having the strength to rule; 'Nobody from his house could take over' removes that qualification.
